sentences.text: It is common knowledge that from March 2020 onwards, owing to Covid-19 pandemic onslaught, no effective judicial steps could be taken by any of the litigants.
sentences._hearing_file: Unknown vs The District Collector on 17 April, 2023.json

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court was deeply conscious of this particular fact and therefore, had suo motu extended period of limitation which would have fallen during the period of Covid-19 pandemic till 28.02.2022.

sentences.text: By the impugned order, the first respondent had rejected that particular request stating that it had been presented after the statutory period as stipulated under Section 64 of the said Act, which provided that such representation must be given within a period of six months and the District Collector has authority to extend the period or rather condone the delay for a further period of one year, but it must be kept in mind that the period came right in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic.

sentences.text: The only https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis issue was with respect to Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences._hearing_file: Unknown vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The entire issue arose Section 64 of the said Act, which is extracted hereunder:
64.Reference to Authority.-(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be,
whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested:
Provided that the Collector shall, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of application, make a reference to the appropriate Authority:
Provided further that where the Collector fails to make such reference within the period so specified, the applicant may apply to the Authority, as the case may be,
requesting it to direct the Collector to make the reference to it within a period of thirty days.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made-- (a) person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis weeks from the date of the Collectors award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 21, or within six months from the date of the Collectors award,
whichever period shall first expire:

Provided further that the Collector may entertain an application after the expiry of the said period, within a further period of one year, if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within the period specified in the first proviso.
3.The said provision, gives authority to the Collector to, on receipt of an application,
to make a reference.

sentences.text: Though time limit has been given, there is also a proviso which stipulates that the Collector may entertain the applications after the expiry of the said period and within a further period of one year.

sentences.text: 4.The learned counsel for the petitioners placed reliance on an earlier order in W.P(MD)No.15207 of 2022, Muthulakshmi and others-vs-The District https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Collector, Trichy and another.

sentences.text: The said order has to be passed on the basis of the representation already given.

sentences.text: With respect to the period of limitation, the aforementioned directions may be followed and to avoid any technicalities, a direction is given to the petitioners herein to forward a fresh representation, copy of the original application afresh, enclosing a copy of this order

sentences.text: and if it is so, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, then the issue of limitation need not be stressed by the District Collector.

sentences.text: 5.In view of the above, the writ petition is allowed.

opennyai_summary.17_April_2023__facts:
The writ petition has been filed in the nature of a Certiorarified Mandamus seeking interference with an order, dated 10.11.2021 in Na.Ka.No.C1/11086/2013 of the first respondent / District https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Collector, Trichy, and consequently direct the said respondent to refer the issues relating to grant of compensation to the petitioners herein for land acquired to the appropriate authority namely, the Principal District Court, Trichy, as provided under Section 64 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
2.
The award in the present case was passed on 17.07.2019.
It is common knowledge that from March 2020 onwards, owing to Covid-19 pandemic onslaught, no effective judicial steps could be taken by any of the litigants.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court was deeply conscious of this particular fact and therefore, had suo motu extended period of limitation which would have fallen during the period of Covid-19 pandemic till 28.02.2022.
opennyai_summary.17_April_2023__decision:
By the impugned order, the first respondent had rejected that particular request stating that it had been presented after the statutory period as stipulated under Section 64 of the said Act, which provided that such representation must be given within a period of six months and the District Collector has authority to extend the period or rather condone the delay for a further period of one year, but it must be kept in mind that the period came right in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic.
In view of this particular fact and in view of the further fact that the Hon'ble Supreme Court themselves had taken up these issues suo motu and had come to the rescue of every litigant /citizen across the country, the order of the first respondent / District Collector, Trichy, is set aside and the matter is remitted back to the District Collector, who may issue notice to the petitioners herein and thereafter, examine the order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court as provided in suo motu Writ Petition (C) No.3 of 2020 In RE: Cognizance for Extension of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Limitation,
dated 10.01.2022, whereby, the limitation was extended till 28.02.2022.
The District Collector, if he/she is satisfied that the petitioners have made every endeavour to seek reference of the award before the competent authority /Principal District Court, Trichy, may, without any further delay refer the matter to the Principal District Court, Trichy, for further proceedings in manner know to law and in accordance with the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
5. The writ petition stands allowed.
The impugned order of the District Collector is set aside and the District Collector is directed to pass fresh orders on the representation already given without putting to the disadvantage of the petitioners the issue of limitation within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.

opennyai_summary.19_June_2023__facts:
The writ petition has been filed seeking the relief in the nature of certiorarified mandamus seeking interference with an order of the first respondent, the District Collector, Trichy, and to consequently direct the said first respondent to refer the matter relating to acquisition of land of the petitioners herein to the appropriate Court, so as to enable the petitioners to get enhanced compensation for the Unknown vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023
Claiming that the stipulations under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
had not been followed, the petitioners had presented representation before the District Collector,
Trichy to refer the entire issue before the competent Court.
The only https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis issue was with respect to Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The entire issue arose Section 64 of the said Act, which is extracted hereunder:
64.Reference to Authority.-(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be,
whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested:
Provided that the Collector shall, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of application, make a reference to the appropriate Authority:
Provided further that where the Collector fails to make such reference within the period so specified, the applicant may apply to the Authority, as the case may be,
requesting it to direct the Collector to make the reference to it within a period of thirty days.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made-- (a) person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis weeks from the date of the Collectors award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 21, or within six months from the date of the Collectors award,
whichever period shall first expire:
Unknown vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54004697/
3
By an order, dated 17.04.2023 in similar issue, this Court had held that in view of this particular provision which had not been examined by the District Collector, the order impugned should be set aside and fresh orders have to be passed.
opennyai_summary.19_June_2023__decision:
The time limits may be examined by the District Collector in each one of the cases and in each one of the cases that the petitioners give necessary reason for delay and if the District Collector is satisfied with the delay, then he may refer the matter to the competent Court, then the District Court at Trichy.
The said order has to be passed on the basis of the representation already given.
With respect to the period of limitation, the aforementioned directions may be followed and to avoid any technicalities, a direction is given to the petitioners herein to forward a fresh representation, copy of the original application afresh, enclosing a copy of this order
and if it is so, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, then the issue of limitation need not be stressed by the District Collector.
5.In view of the above, the writ petition is allowed.
